The cited answer is saved at `results/knowledge_base_answer.md`. Nothing was run on the TPU VM. Summary of what the knowledge base returned:

**1. Per-chip v6e HBM and bandwidth**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| HBM per chip | 32 GB (TPU7x table labels it 32 GiB) |
| HBM bandwidth per chip | 1638 GBps |

Sources: the Cloud TPU v6e doc and TPU7x doc, with the scaling-book spec table agreeing at 32 GiB and 1.6e12 bytes/s.[^v6e][^7x][^sb] No source states how much of the 32 GB is left for user tensors after runtime and communication-stack allocations.[^v6e-page]

**2. v6e-4 chips and total HBM**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Chips in `ct6e-standard-4t` (v6e-4, topology 2x2) | 4 (half of an 8-chip host) |
| Total HBM | 128 GB, derived as 4 x 32 GB |

The per-slice total is arithmetic, not a stated figure.[^v6e] It is four separate 32 GB HBMs, one per chip, not a pool. An unsharded IG batch must fit in one chip's 32 GB.[^sb]

**3. torch_tpu memory API**

Yes. The TorchTPU public-API list marks the `torch.accelerator` memory functions as stable for TPU: `memory_allocated`, `memory_reserved`, `max_memory_allocated`, `max_memory_reserved`, `memory_stats`, `reset_peak_memory_stats`, `get_memory_info`, and `empty_cache`.[^pub] There is no `torch.tpu.memory_*` API. The static capacity properties `hbm_bytes_per_chip` and `hbm_bytes_per_device` are experimental, and `total_memory` is deprecated as of TorchTPU 0.2.1.[^pub][^api] The `torch.accelerator` APIs require PyTorch 2.11 or newer.[^api] Neither torch_tpu page states what "reserved" means for the PJRT allocator or whether figures are per chip or per device.

Practical implication for IG sizing: budget each sharded shard against one chip's 32 GB, read `max_memory_allocated` after a run to measure peak, and sweep `n_steps` from there.

[^v6e]: https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/v6e
[^7x]: https://docs.cloud.google.com/tpu/docs/tpu7x
[^sb]: https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/tpus/
[^v6e-page]: Installed knowledge-base page `pages/hw/v6e/overview.md`
[^pub]: https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/blob/main/docs/public_apis.md
[^api]: https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu/blob/main/docs/api_reference.md
